      The harbor survey began in the spring, when the ice had cleared from the inner channel and 
      the pilots could take the launch out at first light. Each morning the crew measured the depth at

      breakwater, and the shoal off the old ferry landing had grown by almost a meter. The pilots had 
      known this for years from the feel of the boats, but the survey gave them numbers they could 
      show the port council.

      Classification: UNCLASSIFIED
      Date: 15 January 2026
      Report ID: FR-2026-0115-ALPHA
      EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
      This report documents observations from recent field surveys conducted across 
      multiple regions. Teams were deployed to verify infrastructure conditions and 
      document geographic reference points for future operations.
      SECTION 1: NORTHERN SURVEY AREA
      Survey Team Alpha conducted reconnaissance of the northern sector on 12 January 
      2026. The team departed base camp at 0600 hours and proceeded to the following 
      waypoints:
      Primary observation post established at MGRS 18SUJ2337006519. This location 
      provides excellent visibility of the surrounding terrain. Elevation approximately 
      342 meters above sea level. Weather conditions were clear with visibility exceeding 
      10 kilometers.
      Secondary checkpoint located at 18S UJ 28450 12380. This position marks the 
      intersection of two major supply routes. Infrastructure appears to be in good 
      condition with recent maintenance evident.
      Team reported wildlife activity near grid reference 18SUJ1985003421. Several deer 
      were observed grazing in the open meadow. No signs of human activity in the 
      immediate area.
      SECTION 2: EASTERN CORRIDOR
      Survey Team Bravo was tasked with mapping the eastern corridor. Operations 
      commenced on 13 January 2026 at 0530 hours.
      Initial waypoint: 33UUP0511090085
      This location serves as the primary communication relay point. Equipment check 
      confirmed all systems operational. Battery levels at 87%.
      The team proceeded along the designated route, documenting conditions at the 
      following coordinates:
      - Checkpoint Echo: 33U UP 08234 92156
      - Checkpoint Foxtrot: 33UUP1245095320
      - Checkpoint Golf: 33U UP 15670 88940
      Road conditions between checkpoints were noted as follows:
      - Echo to Foxtrot: Paved, good condition, minor debris
      - Foxtrot to Golf: Gravel, moderate washout damage, passable with caution
      SECTION 3: SOUTHERN BOUNDARY
      Team Charlie surveyed the southern boundary region on 14 January 2026. This area 
      presents unique challenges due to varied terrain.
      Boundary marker Alpha located at MGRS 4QFJ1234567890. Marker is intact and clearly 
      visible. GPS coordinates verified against topographic maps.
      The following points of interest were documented:

      testing before consumption.

      Radio contact was intermittent in this approximately 3 kilometer stretch. Terrain 
      features likely cause of interference.
      SECTION 4: WESTERN HIGHLANDS
      Team Delta conducted aerial reconnaissance of the western highlands using unmanned 
      aerial systems on 15 January 2026.
      Launch site established at 15SWC4521078340. Conditions optimal for flight 
      operations with winds less than 10 knots.
      Notable observations:
      1. Large gathering of vehicles at 15S WC 52340 81250 - approximately 25 vehicles, 
      appears to be commercial activity
      2. Forest fire damage visible at 15SWC6012073890 - estimated 40 hectares affected, 
      no active burning
      3. New construction at 15S WC 48900 85120 - residential development, approximately 
      12 structures in progress
      Flight path covered the following grid squares:
      15SWC45, 15SWC46, 15SWC55, 15SWC56, 15SWC65, 15SWC66
      Total flight time: 4 hours 23 minutes
      Images captured: 1,247
      Area covered: approximately 180 square kilometers
      SECTION 5: EQUIPMENT STATUS
      All survey equipment performed within specifications. The following maintenance 
      items are noted:
      - GPS Unit Serial 4472: Battery replacement required, accuracy verified at 
      18SUJ2500010000
      - Radio Set Charlie-7: Antenna damaged, temporary repair in place, full replacement 
      recommended
      - Vehicle 3 (Callsign Hammer): Oil change due at next scheduled maintenance
      CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS
      1. Northern sector infrastructure remains in good condition
      2. Eastern corridor requires road maintenance between Foxtrot and Golf
      3. Southern boundary water source should be tested and potentially developed
      4. Western highlands construction activity should be monitored
      5. Communication relay at 33UUP0511090085 requires backup power installation

      18SUJ2337006519 - Northern OP

Project Phoenix - Sprint Planning Meeting
Date: January 8, 2026
Attendees: Sarah Chen (PM), Mike Rodriguez (Tech Lead), Lisa Park (Designer), Tom Harris (Backend)

AGENDA ITEMS
============

1. Sprint 14 Retrospective Summary
----------------------------------
- Velocity improved by 15% compared to Sprint 13
- Deployment pipeline issues resolved by DevOps team
- Customer feedback integration process needs refinement
- Action item: Lisa to create feedback dashboard mockups

2. Sprint 15 Goals
------------------
Priority 1: Complete user authentication refactor
  - Migrate from session-based to JWT tokens
  - Implement refresh token rotation
  - Estimated: 8 story points
  - Owner: Tom Harris

Priority 2: Dashboard redesign implementation
  - New widget system with drag-and-drop
  - Dark mode support
  - Estimated: 13 story points
  - Owner: Lisa Park

Priority 3: API rate limiting
  - Redis-based token bucket implementation
  - Admin configuration interface
  - Estimated: 5 story points
  - Owner: Mike Rodriguez

3. Technical Debt Discussion
----------------------------
- Database query optimization needed for reports module
- Legacy notification service migration to be scheduled for Sprint 16
- Unit test coverage target: increase from 72% to 80%

4. Blockers and Risks
---------------------
- Waiting on security audit results (expected Jan 12)
- Third-party payment provider API update may require changes
- New team member onboarding may impact velocity

NEXT MEETING: January 15, 2026 at 10:00 AM
